historical_growth.growth_rate_source: bvps_5yr_cagr (FY2020 C$37.0 -> FY2025 C$73.0 on year-end shares). Book value per share rather than total equity, because total-equity growth (19.3%) is inflated by equity issued as acquisition currency.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 3yr CAGR 27.1% vs equity 3yr CAGR 17.9% (>30% divergence): FY2022 EPS was depressed by acquisition and financing costs and FY2025 EPS includes lower net financing expense; all of these CAGRs are acquisition-driven (organic net revenue growth has run ~5-8%), and the DCF projects organic growth only after FY2027.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = company-defined FCF (post-lease, pre-interest) less equity-settled option expense: FY2020 732.1, FY2022 304.5, FY2025 1,711.7. Extremely noisy because of working-capital swings (DSO normalisation 2022, receivables factoring 2025), so the FCF CAGRs are not used. SBC is ~0.02% of net revenue, so owner and reported FCF CAGRs are essentially equal - no SBC creep.

scenario_narratives.base: WSP hits the midpoint of its FY2026 guide (net revenues C$16.6bn, adjusted EBITDA C$3.14bn), integrates TRC on plan and grows ~5% organically, consistent with the record C$20.1bn backlog and 5.7% organic backlog growth. Adjusted margin edges to ~19.5% while integration/reorganisation/ERP charges, which WSP excludes from adjusted EBITDA but which recur for a serial acquirer, settle near 0.9% of net revenue. Leverage returns inside the 1-2x target by FY2027 from internal cash flow. No future acquisitions are credited.
scenario_narratives.bull: The axes break WSP's way: TRC's US power and grid franchise keeps growing double-digit, data-centre, water and energy-transition programmes keep organic growth ~7% for five years, and AI tooling shows up as higher utilisation and margin rather than lower fees (adjusted margin ~20.5%). The market re-rates the stock back toward its historical 15-18x EBITDA range, reflected in a 20x terminal FCF cap.
scenario_narratives.bear: The market's current worry is right: generative design and automation compress the billable-hour model that underpins engineering consultancy fees, US infrastructure funding fades after the IIJA cycle, and Europe/APAC stay weak (APAC is already contracting organically). Organic growth runs ~1%, owner EBITDA margin falls ~1.5pp as utilisation drops and restructuring recurs, leverage stays above target, and the exit multiple de-rates to 13x. A renewed, larger Arcadis pursuit funded with equity at depressed prices is an additional, unmodelled downside.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on NET revenue for a Canadian engineering consultancy: leases charged as operating cost (treatment B, liabilities out of net debt), integration/restructuring/ERP costs charged as recurring despite being excluded from WSP's adjusted EBITDA, near-zero SBC (share units are cash-settled and already in EBITDA), TRC included via FY2026 guidance and the post-deal balance sheet, and no credit for future M&A. CAD WACC 7.75% identical across scenarios; risk carried in the scenario flows and a bear-tilted 25/50/25 weighting.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI/automation deflating billable-hour fees in design and engineering services - the axis the market is currently pricing.
US infrastructure funding cycle after IIJA expiry; US is now the largest region after TRC.

Leverage 2.3x net debt/adjusted EBITDA (Q2-2026) and appetite for further large M&A (rejected Arcadis approach at EUR 51.50/share); a large equity-funded deal at today's price would dilute the per-share value.
Integration execution on TRC and Ricardo; acquisition/integration costs ran C$181m in H1-2026 alone.
The model credits no future acquisitions, which understates value if WSP keeps buying accretively, as it historically has.
Terminal value is roughly 60% of enterprise value; the 18x cap binds in the base case.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 156.64-290.23.
data_sources.financials: WSP Global FY2015-FY2025 annual reports and Q1-2015 to Q2-2026 interim MD&A/financial statements (research/WSP.TO/Extracted/); Metrics.csv in CAD millions. Net debt, lease liabilities and diluted shares from the Q2-2026 interim statements (26-Jun-2026); FY2026 guidance from the Q2-2026 investor presentation.
data_sources.qualitative: Q2-2026 MD&A key events (TRC closing Feb-2026, Arcadis proposal and rejection July 2026), segment reviews, and the FY2025 annual report notes on share-based payments and leases. Analysis.json was not yet available.

inputs.revenue_basis: NET revenues (gross revenues less subconsultant and direct pass-through costs). FY2025 net revenues C$13,959.1m vs gross C$18,285.0m. WSP guides, reports margins and sets targets on net revenues, so every driver path (EBITDA margin, lease, D&A, capex) is a percent of NET revenue. The Metrics.csv Revenue column is gross; do not divide these margins into it.
inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted average shares Q2-2026 (135,004,193 for the quarter; 135,038,672 six months), Q2-2026 interim FS. 134.82m basic at 24-Feb-2026 after the Dec-2025 C$949m equity raise that part-funded TRC. Held FLAT: SBC is essentially nil (equity-settled options C$2.4m FY2025) and the redeemable share units (max 582,739 shares) are liability-accounted and already expensed in personnel costs inside adjusted EBITDA, so counting them as shares too would double-charge. No buybacks (buyback_cash 0) - the flat count is a convention the company funds only by not issuing; equity issuance has historically been acquisition currency (FY2024 C$1,115.8m, FY2025 C$949.0m) and is not modelled because acquisitions beyond TRC are not modelled.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report note on share-based payments: equity-settled stock-option expense C$2.4m (C$6.0m FY2024). The C$72.8m of share-unit plan cost (PSU/RSU/DSU, cash-settled or holder-choice redeemable) is a liability-accounted CASH cost already inside personnel costs and adjusted EBITDA, so it is not added back and not charged again. No net-share-settlement tax line exists (EquityAwardTaxes = 0).
inputs.interest_income_note: Not deducted. WSP is a net debtor (net debt C$6.89bn) and its operating cash flow is stated before net financing expense (net financing expenses paid sit in financing activities), so interest income (C$10.0m FY2025) is not inside reported FCF.
inputs.reported_fcf_definition: Company-defined free cash flow FY2025 = cash from operations C$2,246.0m - lease payments C$384.7m - net capex C$147.2m = C$1,714.1m (FY2025 MD&A s.9.1). Pre-interest (financing expenses paid sit in financing), post-lease. Flattered by a C$325.5m working-capital inflow including C$195.0m of receivables factoring in Q1-2025; TTM to Q2-2026 is C$1.40bn, which is close to the component build's normalised level.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T20:00:00Z regular close (TSX, Friday; latest available on 2026-10-11)
inputs.wacc_rationale: CAD-built. Government of Canada 10y ~3.3%; equity risk premium 5.5%; beta ~0.95 (professional services, government/infrastructure-weighted client base, but acquisitive and now 2.3x levered) -> cost of equity ~8.5%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% (CAD/USD senior unsecured notes and term loans), after 26% tax ~3.7%. Market weights at the current price: equity ~C$22.1bn, net debt ~C$6.9bn -> D/V ~24%. WACC ~7.3%; set at 7.75% as a round, slightly conservative rate and held IDENTICAL across scenarios - AI-disruption, infrastructure-cycle and integration risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate (charge risk once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: full lease cash payments (principal + interest; C$384.7m FY2025 = 2.76% of net revenue; C$206.6m H1-2026 = 2.59%) charged via lease_cost_pct_path at 2.65%, and lease liabilities (C$1,247.6m at 26-Jun-2026: 310.0 current + 937.6 non-current) EXCLUDED from net debt. da_pct_path is depreciation of property & equipment plus amortisation of non-acquisition intangibles only (C$150.9m + C$53.7m = 1.47% FY2025), i.e. EX right-of-use depreciation, so the lease is not charged twice in cash-tax EBIT. This matches WSP's own FCF and net-debt definitions.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are immaterial (-C$0.5m FY2025 earnings share); no adjustment.
inputs.non_adjusted_costs_treatment: Adjusted EBITDA excludes acquisition, integration and reorganisation costs (C$185.4m FY2025, C$133.8m FY2024, C$181.0m in H1-2026 alone on TRC) and ERP implementation costs (C$65.2m FY2025). For a serial acquirer these recur, so ebitda_margin_path is OWNER EBITDA = adjusted EBITDA margin less these charges: FY2025 18.35% - 1.80% = 16.55%; FY2026 guidance midpoint 18.9% less ~2.1% (TRC integration + ERP) = 16.8%; settling to ~0.9% ongoing charge against a ~19.5% adjusted margin from FY2029.
inputs.acquisitions_treatment: TRC Companies (closed Feb-2026, ~US$3.3bn incl. US$1.0bn debt repaid) is IN the model: its revenue is in FY2026/FY2027 growth and its debt is in the 26-Jun-2026 net debt. Future M&A is OUT: WSP has compounded largely by acquisition, but each deal's purchase price is a cash/equity outflow that would offset the acquired FCF; the model assumes future M&A is NPV-neutral and projects organic growth only after FY2027. This is conservative relative to WSP's record of value-accretive deals. The rejected Arcadis approach (EUR 51.50/share, rejected 30-Jul-2026, non-binding) is not modelled.
inputs.working_capital_note: wc_capture -5% of the revenue increase (growth consumes receivables/contract assets; DSO 71 days at Q2-2026). Applied uniformly by the engine, so FY2026 is overcharged by ~C$100m because TRC's working capital was bought with the deal (and is in net debt); left in deliberately as an offset to H1-2026 FCF weakness from POWER Engineers retention-award payments.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company: engineering and professional-services consultancy, ~73,000+ staff, Canada/Americas/EMEIA/APAC). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'Operating company, non-US' -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md (CAD WACC, lease treatment B, SBC-near-zero). Not a bank/REIT/LIC/holdco/distressed shell. No prior DCF or MEMORY.md entry exists - fresh build. Analysis.json was not present when this was built; scenario axes taken from filings and market context. FY2026 guidance (Q2-2026 presentation, revised): net revenues C$16.2-17.0bn (mid C$16.6bn, +18.9% incl. TRC), adjusted EBITDA C$3.10-3.18bn (mid 18.9% margin). Q2-2026 leverage 2.3x net debt/adjusted EBITDA vs 1.0-2.0x target, guided back inside by year-end. Share-unit cash liability (C$122.5m vested at Dec-2025) is partly hedged by deferred-compensation securities and is left out of the bridge (~C$0.9/share). Pension obligations not bridged (small). SBC is near zero, so house and street values nearly coincide; band_position is not meaningful.
inputs.data_vintage: Price 2026-10-09 close; balance sheet and share count Q2-2026 interim (26-Jun-2026); flows FY2025 annual; guidance Q2-2026 presentation (5-Aug-2026).

bear.narrative: Below the FY2026 range, then near-zero organic growth: generative design and automation deflate billable-hour fees, US federal infrastructure funding fades after the IIJA cycle, and UK/APAC stay soft. Owner EBITDA margin compresses ~1.5pp as utilisation falls and right-sizing costs recur; the exit multiple de-rates to 13x.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 = guidance midpoint C$16.6bn net revenue (+18.9%, ~13pp acquisition from TRC/Ricardo, ~5% organic). FY2027 +6.5% = ~5% organic plus TRC's January stub. Then organic only, 5% fading to 2.5% (nominal infrastructure/energy-transition spend; backlog C$20.1bn, 11.6 months, organic backlog +5.7% YoY).
base.margin_rationale: Owner EBITDA = adjusted EBITDA less acquisition/integration/reorganisation and ERP costs. Adjusted margin 18.35% FY2025 -> 18.9% FY2026 guide -> ~19.5% by FY2029 (Q2-2026 printed 19.1%, +90bps YoY on US/Canada productivity); recurring non-adjusted charges ~2.1% FY2026 (TRC) falling to ~0.9%.
base.tax_rationale: Unlevered cash tax on EBIT (interest shield sits in WACC). FY2025 ETR 26.4%; cash taxes C$379.6m on modelled EBIT ~C$1.72bn = 22% levered, ~25-26% after adding back the interest shield. 25% flat.
base.narrative: WSP delivers its FY2026 guide, absorbs TRC and grows mid-single-digit organically on US power/grid, water and transport demand, with adjusted margins drifting up ~60bps on productivity and the TRC mix. No further M&A is credited.

bull.narrative: Top of the FY2026 range, then 7% organic growth as US grid/power (TRC), data-centre and water spend compounds and AI tooling lifts consultant productivity faster than it compresses fees; adjusted margin reaches ~20.5% with integration charges fading.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the share price has fallen ~42% from its 52-week high on a genuine, unresolved debate about AI deflating consultancy fees, leverage is 2.3x (above target) after TRC, and management has shown appetite for a further large deal (Arcadis). Base 50% is anchored by guidance just raised at the low end and a record backlog. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things - sustained 7% organic growth, margin expansion and a re-rating - to go right together.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
